newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac warns against early retirement.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac warns against early retirement.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac has warned his compatriots that a wave of labour unrest pressing for a reduction of the retirement age from 60 to 55 flew in the face of international economic realities.

"Our compatriots wish to work less and retire earlier and I understand this," Chirac said late on Saturday at a banquet for him in this village in central France where he owns the local chateau and where his wife is deputy mayor.
"But I hope that our country will not forget the economic and demographic realites of the world we live in. We can do better if we work better, that is true.
"But we will not do better if an ever decreasing number of working people have to carry the weight of an increasing number of youths and retired people," he said.
Truckers seeking a 55-year-old retirement age and other advantages staged a 12-day strike in November which crippled traffic throughout France and seriously hampered the economy.
The government gave in to many of their demands, sparking a wave of similar, if less effective, strikes since in other sectors of the economy.
The government is now also trying to introduce a youth job training scheme it says will provide more jobs for the young but which unions says is really aimed at getting around minimum wage laws.
